natural_language: Solve a multi-period (time-coupled) optimal power flow scheduling problem on the MATPOWER test system case22. The base network data are first modified as follows: (i) set the reactive demand at bus 8 to zero (QD = 0), (ii) set the minimum reactive power capability of the generator at bus 1 to QMIN = -50 MVAr, (iii) double the series resistance BR_R of the branch whose from-bus is 11 and to-bus is 19, and (iv) scale the total line charging susceptance BR_B of the branch whose from-bus is 22 and to-bus is 1 by 1.1. The scheduling problem is then formulated over multiple time periods using demand and renewable generation profiles, producing an expected dispatch and corresponding marginal prices across time. In addition to standard production costs, augment the objective with a quadratic penalty on phase angle differences across all branches in each time period, proportional to the squared 2-norm of the vector of angle differences (i.e., penalize large |Va_from − Va_to| over the network) using a user-specified penalty weight beta. The OPF feasibility tolerance must be tightened by setting opf_violation to 1e-6. Implement the multi-period formulation using MOST (MATPOWER Optimal Scheduling Tool) with a DC network model, and configure solver/verbosity options appropriately to ensure reliable convergence under the tighter feasibility tolerance.

objective_modification.name: phase_angle_difference_penalty
objective_modification.form: Sum_t beta * ||E * Va(t)||_2^2, where E maps bus angles to branch angle differences (Va_from - Va_to)

constraint_modification.name: multi_period_scheduling
constraint_modification.form: MOST multi-period dispatch with time-varying load/renewable profiles (and any xGen ramp/capability constraints provided by xgd)

natural_language:
Solve a multi-period optimal power flow (OPF) on the MATPOWER test case "case22" over a time horizon defined by time-varying profiles. The model is a DC multi-period economic dispatch/OPF (i.e., linearized power flow with voltage magnitudes fixed and phase angles as the network state) with generator operating limits enforced each period. The objective is the expected total operating cost over all periods, augmented with an additional quadratic penalty on branch-to-branch phase angle differences to discourage large angle separations across connected buses. Specifically, an angle-difference penalty term is added each period in the form beta * ||E * Va(t)||_2^2, where Va(t) is the vector of bus voltage angles in period t and E is the branch incidence-difference operator built from (from_bus, to_bus) connectivity.

Before building the multi-period model, apply the following parameter modifications to the base case data: (1) set the reactive demand at bus 8 to zero by scaling QD to 0; (2) set the generator reactive lower limit QMIN at bus 1 to -50 MVAr; (3) double the series resistance BR_R for the branch from bus 11 to bus 19; and (4) scale the total line charging susceptance BR_B by 1.1 for the branch from bus 22 to bus 1.

Use MOST (MATPOWER Optimal Scheduling Tool) to construct and solve the multi-period DC model from the modified base network plus generator/ramping data and time-varying profiles. Configure the solver tolerances such that OPF constraint violation tolerance is 1e-6. Use a DC network model setting in MOST, and solve the resulting quadratic program (due to the added quadratic angle-difference penalty) with an appropriate QP-capable solver (e.g., MIPS where applicable, or another available QP solver).

objective_modification.name: phase_angle_difference_penalty
objective_modification.form: sum_t beta * ||E * Va(t)||_2^2 (implemented as quadratic cost on Va each period)

natural_language:
Solve a security-constrained AC optimal power flow (SC-ACOPF) on the MATPOWER test case “case22”. The model must include standard AC power flow physics (voltage magnitudes and angles, active/reactive power balances), generator real/reactive limits, bus voltage limits, and branch thermal limits as defined in the case file.

Apply the following data (parameter) modifications prior to solving: (1) set the reactive load at bus 8 to zero (QD scaled to 0); (2) set the generator at bus 1 reactive minimum limit QMIN to −50 MVAr; (3) for the branch from bus 11 to bus 19, scale the series resistance BR_R by a factor of 2; and (4) for the branch from bus 22 to bus 1, scale the total line charging susceptance BR_B by a factor of 1.1.

To ensure feasibility under stressed conditions, explicitly model load shedding. For every bus with positive active demand (PD > 0), add a dedicated “load-shedding generator” whose active power output represents curtailed load at that bus. Each such shedding variable must be bounded between 0 and the original PD at that bus, and it must not provide reactive power (QMIN = QMAX = 0). The objective must penalize load shedding using a convex quadratic polynomial cost (per shedding generator) so that shedding is only used when necessary.

In addition to the standard generation cost and the load-shedding penalty, augment the objective with a voltage-stability term based on the L-index. Compute the L-index using the network admittance matrix partitioned into generator-bus and load-bus subsets, and add a weighted penalty proportional to the maximum L-index over all PQ (load) buses. This produces an ACOPF objective that trades off production cost, load curtailment, and voltage stability.

Impose N−1 security constraints on branch active power flows using a DC linearized post-contingency approximation: for each in-service branch with a nonzero RATE_A, consider its outage as a contingency and enforce that all monitored in-service, limited branches respect their RATE_A limits under the resulting post-contingency flows. These post-contingency flows must be computed using PTDF/LODF sensitivities and enforced as additional linear constraints on bus voltage angles.

Use a tight OPF feasibility tolerance opf.violation = 1e−6. Use MIPS as the solver (AC model), with standard MATPOWER output controls as desired. Implement the optimization using MATPOWER’s OPF model constructor and extensions (OPF_MODEL), adding nonlinear cost for the L-index term and linear constraints for the N−1 security limits; load shedding is implemented by augmenting the case with additional generators and corresponding costs. Finally, solve the resulting SC-ACOPF and report feasibility, objective value, total shed load, and the resulting L-index metrics. Set solver options to enforce the specified violation tolerance and use the AC formulation with MIPS.

structural_modification.problem: Security-Constrained ACOPF (ACOPF with DC N-1 line-flow security constraints)

objective_modification.name: load_shedding_generators_and_cost
objective_modification.form: For each load bus k: add variable Lshed_k via a synthetic generator with 0 <= Lshed_k <= PD_k, Q=0, and add convex quadratic penalty sum_k (c2_k*Lshed_k^2 + c1_k*Lshed_k + c0_k).

objective_modification.name: voltage_stability_L_index_cost
objective_modification.form: Add lambda_L * L_max(V), where L_max is the maximum L-index over PQ buses computed from F = -Y_LL^{-1} Y_LG and complex voltages V.

constraint_modification.name: N1_security_constraints
constraint_modification.form: LODF-based post-contingency active line-flow limits enforced as linear constraints on Va for each single line outage of in-service branches with RATE_A > 0 (monitored set identical).

natural_language:
Formulate and solve a DC security-constrained optimal power flow (DC-SCOPF) on the MATPOWER test system case118. The base network data are taken from case118, with a parameter adjustment applied prior to optimization: the shunt susceptance (BS) at bus 78 is set to −0.1 (in per-unit on the system base). The optimization minimizes the standard MATPOWER DC OPF generation cost subject to DC power balance, generator operating limits, and standard branch flow constraints.

In addition, impose explicit N−1 transmission security constraints for single-line outages using LODF-based post-contingency flow expressions. The contingency set consists of all in-service branches that have a positive continuous rating (RATE_A > 0). For each contingency (outage of one such branch), enforce that every in-service, rate-limited branch respects its RATE_A limit in both directions under the corresponding post-contingency flows.

Solve using a DC OPF formulation with a tight feasibility tolerance by setting the OPF violation tolerance to 1e−6. Use MATPOWER’s OPF model construction interface to add the N−1 linear constraints, and run with a DC solver (e.g., MIPS) under the specified verbosity/output settings.

constraint_modification.name: N1_security_constraints
constraint_modification.form: LODF-based post-contingency branch flow limits for all single outages of in-service branches with RATE_A > 0; enforce |f_ell^(k)| <= RATE_A_ell for all monitored lines ell and contingencies k

natural_language:
Solve a DC optimal transmission switching (DC-OTS) optimal power flow for the MATPOWER test case case51ga. The decision problem minimizes the total operating cost, consisting of the standard generator production cost plus additional linear costs for procuring four types of real-power reserves at each generator: up reserve (Ru), down reserve (Rd), spinning reserve (Rs), and non-spinning reserve (Rn). The model co-optimizes generation dispatch, reserve schedules, and line switching decisions.

Before solving, apply these data modifications to the base case: (i) for the generator located at bus 8, scale the quadratic cost coefficient (COST_PARAMS_C3) by 1 and scale the linear cost coefficient (COST_PARAMS_C1) by 1.1; (ii) set the status of branch (5 -> 14) to in-service; and (iii) scale the series reactance of branch (43 -> 5) by 1.2.

The DC-OTS formulation introduces a continuous variable for real power flow on each branch and a binary switching variable per branch that determines whether the branch is available. It replaces the standard DC branch flow equations with big-M linear constraints linking bus voltage angles and branch flows, while also enforcing nodal real power balance using the branch-flow incidence representation. Thermal limits are enforced using linear constraints that bind the branch flow magnitude to the branch status (when a line is switched off, its flow is forced to zero). A system-wide switching budget constraint limits the number of opened lines.

Reserve co-optimization adds generator-level reserve variables (Ru, Rd, Rs, Rn) with (1) upward headroom constraints to ensure Pg + Ru + Rs + Rn does not exceed PMAX, (2) downward capability constraints to ensure Pg − Rd is at least PMIN, and (3) system-wide minimum reserve procurement requirements for each reserve type equal to 1% of the total real power load in the case.

Implementation uses MATPOWER’s OPF modeling layer (OPF model object) to (a) build a DC-OTS mixed-integer linear program via added variables and linear constraints, and (b) add a linear reserve procurement cost to the objective in addition to the default generation cost. Solve using the DC OPF model with an integer-capable solver (e.g., OT via intlinprog). Set the OPF feasibility/violation tolerance to 1e-6 and apply appropriate MILP solver limits (time/nodes) consistent with the provided template.

form: Nodal real power balance via incidence: Cft' * Pf - Cg * Pg = Pd/baseMVA + shunts + injections
Big-M DC flow linking: -M*(1-Z) <= Bf*Va - Pf <= M*(1-Z)
Thermal limits with switching: -RATE_A*Z <= Pf <= RATE_A*Z (in per-unit on baseMVA, with phase shift injections handled)
